items.approach: Astra's r2 amendment adopted: round_trip_ok becomes an ANCHORED match of the whole step text against a closed set of enumerated sentence forms instantiated with the step's own escaped manifest literals. No masking, no sentinels, no generic filler set -- the text must literally contain element.name / window.title (re.escape'd, case-insensitive, internal whitespace as \s+), so a model-supplied '<e>'/'<w>' can never stand in for a manifest field, and only the fixed words of a form may sit between slots, so 'Click the field under Save in the Editor window.' has no form to match. roundtrip.py: _CLICK_WORDS/_TYPE_WORDS keep today's verb lists (roundtrip.py:15-25) as alternations. Building blocks (all optional unless stated): LEAD = (?:the user |you )?(?:double[- ]|right[- ]|left[- ])?; Q = ['"]?; DET = (?:the |a |an |your |on the |on )?; WIN = (?:in|on|within|inside|from) (?:the )?Q{W}Q(?: window| dialog| screen| page| tab)? when window.title is set, else 'in the current window'; CTL = optional one of (button|field|box|textbox|checkbox|menu|item|tab|link|icon|option|list|dropdown|control|element|{control_type}); TARGET when element.name is set = DET Q{E}Q CTL; TARGET when element.name is empty = one of (somewhere|anywhere|here|(?:an?|the) (?:element|control|field|button|item|area|{control_type}|position \(\s*{screen.x},\s*{screen.y}\s*\))) -- coordinates bound to the recorded step.screen.x/y (template.py:26), never free digits; OBJ (type steps only) = (?: (?:a |the )?(?:value|text)(?: in| into)?| in| into)?; TS (type steps) = optional \({text_summary}\) with the literal escaped. Forms, each anchored ^...\.?$ on whitespace-collapsed text, re.IGNORECASE: F1 = LEAD VERB OBJ TARGET WIN TS; F2 (lead-in clause) = (?:In|On|Within|Inside) (?:the )?Q{W}Q(?: window| dialog)?, VERB OBJ TARGET TS. Return (ok, mismatches) where mismatches keeps today's three presence diagnostics ('action' if no own verb word anywhere, 'element' if the element literal is absent, 'window' if the title literal is absent -- the names existing tests assert on) plus 'form' when the presence checks pass but neither form matches. Astra's two probes: 'Click <e> in <w>.' -> element + window (literals absent); 'Click the field under Save in the Editor window.' -> form. Negation ('Do not click ...'), appended clauses (', then delete all records', 'and press Enter'), second sentences, repeated labels, swapped slots and wrong targets all fail the anchor. Every render_step_template form matches (template.py:29-38): "Click the 'Save' Button in the 'SmartDeploy Console' window.", 'Click the position (900, 512) in the ...', 'Click the Edit in the current window.', "Enter a value in the 'Computer name' Edit in the '...' window (entered value in field (content not captured)).", and the backslash title (re.escape). Every stub reply on record matches: 'Click OK in Test Window.' (test_step_generation.py:102), 'The user clicks Save in the SmartDeploy Console window.' after _strip_markdown_emphasis (generation.py:87, :382), 'Click Save in Answer File Editor.' / 'Click somewhere in Answer File Editor.' (test_sidecar_report.py:42-43), 'Click {name} in the {title} window.' (test_step_edits.py:487), 'Click an element in the current window.' / 'Enter a value into Computer name in the X window.' (test_server.py:314-319), 'Click the field in Test Window.' (test_step_generation.py:238-241 for empty-element steps), 'Fill in / Provide / Paste / Set Computer name in Answer File Editor.' (test_roundtrip.py:119-122). generation.py unchanged (any not-ok -> render_step_template). `# ponytail:` comment on the form table names the ceiling: a correct phrasing outside the two forms yields the always-correct template (CLAUDE.md rule 2 permits it); upgrade path is adding a form, never a free filler set. F-10 exemption removal retained: server.py _write_all_exports drops `not verbatim_narration and` before round_trip_ok (server.py:1360-1361) so the step gate applies to polished step text in both build modes; a rejected rewrite reverts to the original text/caption (server.py:1371), never a template. phases/DEVIATIONS.md 'audit-fixes F-10': delete the photo-mode-skip paragraph and its test reference; keep the no-transcript claim-gate paragraph and append one sentence that those rewrites are now covered by A-01's anchored forms.

items.approach: Claims become exactly the strings placed under steps, and placed narration is never LLM-rewritten (the only transformation is the photo flow's deterministic consistency pass, which F-01 runs on the SOURCE before placement, so claims and placed text are the same strings); coverage therefore holds by construction and nothing placed is ever re-dumped. (1) server.py module level: _claims_for_narrative(placed_texts, content): if placed_texts: units = list(placed_texts); else: blocks, _labelled = transcript._parse_text_blocks(content); units = [text for _num, text in blocks] (transcript.py:87/96/100 return a (blocks, labelled) 2-tuple); return extract_claims([{'text': u, 'start': float(i)} for i, u in enumerate(units)]). Drop the _parse_json_segments import from the claims helper (F-01 still imports it for the photo flow). Add _placed_corpus(step_results) = '\n'.join(f"{r.get('text', '')}\n{r.get('narration') or ''}" for r in step_results). (2) _generate: placed = [r['narration'] for r in step_results if r.get('narration')]; content = the transcript text ONLY when transcript_path.suffix.lower() in ('.txt', '.md'), else '' -- a parsed .json transcript is always placed by _place_timed_segments (transcript.py:160-191) so its claims are its placed strings, and a malformed .json already raises inside _apply_transcript (server.py:1733-1736) leaving nothing placed and nothing to claim; raw JSON must never reach extract_claims. With no transcript: placed = [r['text'] for r in step_results], content = '' (synthetic claims are the step texts only; the 'Windows involved' line stays in synthetic_narration for the title prompt but is no longer a claim). claims = _claims_for_narrative(placed, content); placed_text for _narrative_with_coverage = _placed_corpus(step_results). Synthetic claims are always covered by the step corpus, never rendered as [verify], and are still passed unconditionally to _write_all_exports (claims=claims) so A-03's post-polish grounding sees them. (3) Delete narration polish: remove the polish/raw_out parameters and the stage-2 branch from _run_semantic_pipeline (server.py:1669-1719; note becomes f'{n} of {m} step(s) narrated (semantic placement)'); delete src/pipeline/narration_polish.py and tests/pipeline/test_narration_polish.py; remove the placement_meta 'verify_claims' merging in _generate (verify_claim_ids = narrative_verify_ids; claims_by_id from claims; report['transcript_placement'] = placement_meta as-is) and the matching block in _generate_photo (F-01 rewires the rest). items.approach: Deterministic source-text grounding: the narrative is accepted only if it is the claims quoted verbatim, in strictly increasing claim order, each claim consumed AT MOST ONCE, with at most a closed set of leading connectives; anything else is rejected whole and the stage falls back to the existing [verify] path (no token subsets, no synonyms, no polarity heuristics). Astra's r2 amendment adopted: the r1 rule `index >= last matched` let one claim be re-quoted ('Transfer 100 dollars. Then transfer 100 dollars.' matched [0, 0]); the matcher now keeps `pos` = index of the next unconsumed claim and only tries keys with index >= pos, setting pos = index + 1 on a match, so a claim can satisfy one quotation only, omissions are still allowed (skipping forward), and two DISTINCT source claims with identical text are each consumed once in source order. narrative.py: (a) narrative_unsupported(text, claims, allow_verify_lines=False) -> str | None (public, reused post-polish). A line starting with '> [verify]' is never skipped blindly (claim_coverage.py:50 parse_verify_line accepts any such prefix): a verify line is consumed only when allow_verify_lines is True AND line.strip() == render_verify_blockquote(c) for some c in claims (claim_coverage.py:33-34: known id, unaltered text); any other verify line is returned as the unsupported fragment (line[:80]). Remaining lines are joined, rest = _norm(text) (lowercase, collapse whitespace); keys = [(index, _norm(claim text).rstrip(' .!?'))] for non-empty claims; loop: strip leading whitespace/punctuation; candidates = keys with index >= pos, longest text first; if some candidate is a prefix of rest followed by end-of-text or a non-alphanumeric, consume it and set pos = index + 1; elif _CONNECTIVE_RE = ^(?:first|then|next|finally|lastly|afterwards|after that|now)\b[,:]?\s* matches, consume it; else return rest[:80]. Return None when nothing is left. Defeats every counterexample on record: reversal, invented second sentence, conditional dropped, polarity flip, reordering (pos rule), repeated claim (pos rule), and the minted verify line with unknown or valid id. (b) generate_narrative: after the passes, reason = narrative_unsupported(text, claims) (allow_verify_lines=False -- the raw model text precedes ensure_claim_coverage, so no verify line is ever legitimate there); if reason: logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(...) and text = ''; then ensure_claim_coverage(text, claims, placed_text=placed_text) as before (narrative.py:46), so the F-02 failure path and the rejection path are the same path and only ensure_claim_coverage ever mints a verify line. (c) Prompts carry the claims everywhere: _draft_prompt tells the model to use ONLY the listed sentences verbatim, in order, each at most once, optionally omitting some or prefixing 'First,'/'Then,'/'Next,'/'Finally,'; _critique_prompt(draft, claims) and _revise_prompt(draft, critique, claims) embed the same bullet list as 'the only permitted sentences'. (d) server.py _write_all_exports: after the existing owned/validate_claim_coverage safety net (its report key and revert fire first), add: if claims and md_narrative_text and md_narrative_text != narrative_text and (reason := narrative_unsupported(md_narrative_text, claims, allow_verify_lines=True)): report['polish_rejected_narrative'] = reason; md_narrative_text = narrative_text. narrative_text legitimately carries ensure_claim_coverage's blockquotes, so post-polish only the exact render_verify_blockquote(c) lines for known claims pass; a polished, fabricated, re-id'd or duplicated line reverts the whole narrative. Because F-04 always passes claims (synthetic claims = step texts for no-transcript captures), this is the post-polish grounding for synthetic narratives too. `# ponytail:` comment on narrative_unsupported names the ceiling (free prose from the narrative model is rejected whole; upgrade path is a constrained transformation that preserves predicate arguments). Test stubs: _NarrativeGeneratingStub becomes an echo stub returning the '- ' bullet lines of whichever prompt it receives, joined with spaces (grounded by construction, works for passes=3).

items.approach: server.py _generate_photo runs the [narrative] stage exactly like the capture flow and canonicalizes the SOURCE TEXT once, before any placed text, claim or verify line exists. Astra's r2 amendment adopted: canonicalize_terms rewrites whole-word tokens anywhere in a field (consistency.py:283-293, `\b(variant)\b` IGNORECASE), so handing it a serialized .json transcript can rewrite the 'segments' key (Astra's probe: anchor title 'Inspect the Segements collection' turns the key into 'segements' and transcript.py:144 then raises) -- a .json transcript is therefore parsed FIRST and only its segment text values are canonicalized. New order: (1) raw = transcript file text; copy images; models_cfg = load_models_config(...) once (vision_cfg = models_cfg.vision). If matches[0].suffix.lower() == '.json': try segments = _parse_json_segments(raw) except ValueError as exc: segments = []; transcript_note = f'transcript.json ignored: {exc}' (a malformed JSON file places nothing and claims nothing; its syntax never reaches extract_claims). texts = [s['text'] for s in segments] for .json, else [raw]. narration_text = '\n'.join(texts) -- the plain-prose form used for vision context and the title prompt (today caption_images and generate_title_and_overview receive the raw JSON string for .json uploads; this fixes that in passing). caption_images as now with narration_text as context; (2) title only: if not user_title and narration_text.strip(): gen_title, _overview = generate_title_and_overview(narration_text, make_llm_client(), on_screen_texts=...) on the [steps] client, overview discarded, manifest.session.title = gen_title when set; (3) canonicalize_terms([manifest.session.title or '', *texts, *(c or '' for c in captions)], anchor_text=user_title or None, preferred_texts=on_screen_texts) -> write back title, texts and the non-None captions; for .json rebuild narration = json.dumps({'segments': [{'text': t, 'start': s['start']} for s, t in zip(segments, texts)]}) -- text and start are the only fields _parse_json_segments reads (transcript.py:147-150), so the reserialized structure is lossless for placement and no key is ever rewritten; for .txt/.md narration = texts[0]. canonicalize_terms only swaps alphanumeric word tokens (consistency.py:43), so 'Step N:' labels in a .txt/.md are untouched. Persist the title when it differs from user_title (as today, server.py:1204-1217); (4) placement on the CANONICAL narration: if texts are non-empty, align_transcript_to_steps(matches[0].name, narration, manifest) (try/except as today) then the semantic rescue (F-04's polish-free _run_semantic_pipeline; it only fires on the .txt/.md WARNING note, transcript.py:220, so JSON never reaches semantic_align) with caption contexts; (5) step_results exactly as F-03 built them (text = caption or placed or '(no description provided)', used_fallback = caption is None, narration = placed when caption and placed); _assert_1to1_mapping; manually_edited = _apply_manual_edits(...); (6) claims = _claims_for_narrative([per_step[s.id] for s in manifest.steps if per_step.get(s.id)], narration_text) if narration_text.strip() else [] -- for .json narration_text is the joined PARSED segment texts, so the unplaced fallback (F-04's _parse_text_blocks line split) yields one claim per segment and never JSON syntax; delete _narration_to_claims (server.py:129-139) and the except branch that called it (server.py:1168-1172) -- the helper has no remaining callers (tests monkeypatch _claims_for_narrative only, test_server.py:526); (7) narrative_text, narrative_verify_ids = _narrative_with_coverage(claims, _placed_corpus(step_results), models_cfg.narrative.passes) if claims else (None, []) -- draft->critique->revise on make_narrative_llm_client() with A-03's grounding gate and F-02's failure fallback (server.py:1028-1030), identical to captures; (8) report as today but verify_claims = [{'claim_id': cid, 'text': claims_by_id[cid]['text']} for cid in narrative_verify_ids] (one source of ids, no late ensure_claim_coverage, nothing to deduplicate); (9) _write_all_exports(..., narrative_text=narrative_text, claims=claims) so the post-polish coverage and grounding checks are real for photo builds; update its docstring sentence that said the photo call site has no claims. Transcript-derived step text, narration slices, claims, narrative and [verify] quotes all derive from the same canonicalized text values, so the merged spelling tests keep their expectations and no two renderings of the same transcript text can disagree. Remove the stale 'held finding F-01' comment and the manifest-free overview path.
